rationale: This program is a tiny (4417 text bytes, 5 functions), single-purpose numeric benchmark whose execution time is dominated by hot arithmetic loops in planetpv (~80% of the code), so the table favors low-overhead, low-risk transformations: SUB gets the strongest security/diversity weights because instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and especially effective on arithmetic-dense floating-point code like ephemeris math; SPLIT and IGV get high runtime/size tolerance weights since both add negligible overhead to a small binary where every extra byte matters proportionally; IBR and ICALL sit at moderate values to add control-flow and call-site indirection diversity without over-penalizing the hot paths; and BCF and FLA receive the lowest RuntimeCost weights because bogus-control-flow and flattening impose multiplicative slowdowns and size growth that are unacceptable for a compute-bound benchmark with tight loops, while FLA is still retained at a mid security weight so the compiler may flatten only the cold outer function (e.g., main or _start) if its feature profile warrants it. All passes stay enabled with CorrectnessRisk weights kept at or above neutral (0.2-0.6) to preserve validity, prioritizing cheap obfuscation breadth over aggressive heavyweight transformation.
